title: Add workspace [profile.release] block (lto, codegen-units)
description:
The workspace `Cargo.toml` has no `[profile.release]` block, so all release builds inherit Cargo defaults (`lto = false`, `codegen-units = 16`). This prevents cross-crate inlining between `gf2-core` and `gf2-kernels-simd`, forcing every `xor_inplace` / `popcount` / `gf2m_mul` call to go through opaque function-pointer dispatch via `LogicalFns`.

## Background

Empirical profiling on commit `0d2f284` (see `dev/bench_results/2026-04-26-uncompetitiveness-profile.md`): re-running the GF(2) BitMatrix matmul bench with `--features simd` only buys +16% at $n=1024$ and +24% at $n=4096$, vs. ~4× theoretical for `vpxor`-based 256-bit XOR. Most of the SIMD win is consumed by per-call dispatch overhead that LTO would inline away.

This change is foundational for the PPC-spiral epic: it **must land before I1 pins criterion baselines** (`b2ecd2ff`), otherwise every Tier A–E baseline is measured on the wrong profile and every subsequent $\geq 1.5\times$ claim has an artificially low floor.

PPC walk: V0 measure (current bench numbers) → V0' re-measure with optimized profile → record delta. No code changes outside `Cargo.toml`.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] Workspace root `Cargo.toml` has a `[profile.release]` block with `lto = "thin"`, `codegen-units = 1`. `panic = "abort"` is OPTIONAL — defer to user preference.
- [hard] `cargo build --workspace --all-features --release` completes without warnings.
- [hard] `cargo nextest run --workspace --all-features --release --profile ci` passes within the 60 s wall-clock budget (per `CLAUDE.md` test rules).
- [hard] BitMatrix matmul at $n=1024$ (`--features simd`) shows $\geq 1.3\times$ improvement over the no-LTO baseline, captured in `dev/bench_results/2026-04-26-profile-release-delta.md` with measured numbers and host context.
- [hard] No regression on existing benches: every `target/criterion/` baseline that was already passing on commit `0d2f284` stays at the same wall-time geomean ±5% or better.

## Notes

The `lto = "thin"` choice (vs. `"fat"`) is deliberate — fat LTO doubles compile time and gives marginally better inlining only for our pattern. Revisit only if `"thin"` doesn't close the expected gap. Spec doc: `dev/plans/gf2_core_ppc_spiral.md`.
